title: Termination under Optimal Play in the Two-Player 3n+/-1 Game
description: We address the two-player 3n+/-1 problem stated at https://althofer.de/collatz-prizes.html. The game is played on positive odd integers: a move replaces n > 1 by the odd part of either 3n-1 or 3n+1, and the player who reaches 1 wins. Arbitrary play need not terminate. We give a binary normal form, rank finite outcome-proof tokens by a well-founded multiset order, prove the remaining equal-rank routing fibres well-founded, and conclude that no DRAW positions exist. The linked repository contains the complete 138-section proof supplement, standard-library verification code, finite proof certificates, a conditional symbolic certificate for the global routing assembly, negative tests, and a Lean proof of the general certificate metatheorem. The global certificate explicitly retains four human proof obligations and is not represented as a complete formalization of the theorem.
